level: In-depth engineering course · no official exam
name: Mobile Apps with Expo and React Native
audience: Web and TypeScript developers who need to ship and maintain a production iOS and Android app with a small team.
format: This site's course with a 40-question practice test of choose-the-approach, read-the-code and release-and-failure questions.
scenarios: Turning a web product into a mobile app
Shipping a fix to users without a store review
Debugging a slow list or janky animation
Getting through App Store and Google Play review
Handling offline use and flaky networks
verifyNotes: This is the site's own in-depth engineering course, not a vendor certification: there are no exam facts to confirm, so spend Research on finding the best official/primary sources per topic (URLs that will be cited as sources) and on what is current as of November 2026. Goal: a senior engineer or architect who builds products alone or in a team of 2-3 can apply every idea confidently in real work, a design review or a senior interview. Lessons go deep: intuition first, then the precise mechanism, then a fully worked example with real numbers or code, then where it matters in production, then a common misconception. Write math in LaTeX between double dollars only: $$...$$; NEVER single-dollar math (single $ renders literally; in SQL or shell code use code fences). In JSON strings escape backslashes. Markdown tables: never put a raw | inside a cell (escape it as \\| or use \\lvert in math). Every lesson has a hands-on lab: a small exercise with the expected output. State any randomness seed. Code in fenced blocks with the right language. Question mix: ~35% judgment (pick the approach a 1-3 person team can maintain), ~35% read or debug code or config (components, hooks, expo-router files, app.json/app.config, eas.json), ~30% release, store-policy and failure-mode reasoning. Verifiers MUST type-check every TypeScript/TSX example with `sh {{root}}/.pipeline/ts/check.sh <file>` (TypeScript 7.0 strict, Node 24; set NORUN=1 for .tsx or code that needs network; installed: zod 4, react 19, react-native 0.88 types, next 16, vitest 5, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.32, @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.3, jose 6). Expo SDK, EAS Build/Submit/Update and expo-router behaviour cannot be run here: verify against docs.expo.dev line by line and never guess config keys or CLI flags. Store rules (App Store Review Guidelines, Google Play policies, privacy manifests, data safety forms) must come from developer.apple.com and developer.android.com / support.google.com/googleplay with a date. Version-sensitive facts (Expo SDK version, React Native New Architecture status, minimum OS versions, store target-API deadlines) must be dated. Sources: docs.expo.dev, expo.dev, reactnative.dev, react.dev, developer.apple.com, developer.android.com, support.google.com/googleplay, web.dev, developer.mozilla.org, owasp.org (MASVS/MASTG at mas.owasp.org), w3.org; no Medium or vendor-marketing blogs.

domains.name: React Native and Expo foundations
skills: How React Native renders native views: the New Architecture (Fabric, TurboModules, JSI) and what changed from the bridge
Expo vs bare React Native: managed workflow, development builds, prebuild and config plugins, and when you need native code
Core components and styling: View, Text, Image, Pressable, flexbox defaults that differ from the web, platform-specific code
TypeScript project setup, the Metro bundler, environment variables and app config (app.json / app.config.ts)
Debugging: React DevTools, logs, error boundaries and crash reporting

domains.name: Navigation, state and data
skills: expo-router: file-based routes, layouts, stacks, tabs, modals, dynamic routes and deep links / universal links
Server state with TanStack Query: caching, refetch on focus and reconnect, optimistic updates, pagination
Local state and persistence: React state, context, Zustand-style stores, AsyncStorage vs SecureStore vs SQLite
Forms and input on mobile: keyboard handling, validation with Zod, accessibility of inputs
Offline-first: queued mutations, conflict handling, sync on reconnect

domains.name: Native capabilities and platform integration
skills: Permissions model on iOS and Android: requesting at the right moment, handling denial, settings deep links
Push notifications: Expo push service vs APNs/FCM directly, tokens, channels, notification handling in foreground and background
Camera, media library, location and background tasks: battery and policy limits
Secure storage, biometrics and auth flows: OAuth/OIDC with PKCE via the system browser, refresh tokens
Writing a small native module or config plugin when no library exists

domains.name: Performance and user experience
skills: The JS thread vs UI thread, frame budget at 60/120 Hz and what causes jank
Lists: FlatList vs FlashList tuning, keys, getItemLayout, image caching and memory
Animations and gestures: Reanimated worklets and react-native-gesture-handler, running on the UI thread
Startup time and bundle size: Hermes, lazy loading, asset optimisation, measuring with profilers
Accessibility on mobile: VoiceOver and TalkBack, accessibilityRole/Label, dynamic type, touch target sizes, reduced motion

domains.name: Build, release and over-the-air updates
skills: EAS Build profiles, credentials, signing (certificates, provisioning profiles, keystores) and build numbers
Over-the-air updates with EAS Update: runtime versions, channels and branches, rollouts and rollback, what OTA may and may not change under store rules
App Store and Google Play submission: TestFlight, internal/closed testing tracks, review guidelines that commonly cause rejection
Privacy requirements: Apple privacy manifests and nutrition labels, Google Play data safety, account deletion requirements
CI for mobile: automated builds on merge, preview builds for pull requests, versioning strategy

domains.name: Quality, security and operations
skills: Testing pyramid on mobile: Jest with React Native Testing Library, end-to-end with Maestro or Detox
Mobile security per OWASP MASVS: secrets never in the bundle, certificate handling, jailbreak/root realities, secure storage
Crash and performance monitoring, release health and staged rollouts
Supporting old app versions: API versioning, forced-update prompts, feature flags
Choosing between a mobile app, a PWA and a responsive web app for a small team
